description: Source-verified Museum paleodata. Only records with verification.status equal to source_verified are rendered by the app. Modern countries identify fossil collection locations, not reconstructed Mesozoic geography or a complete biological range.

verification.scope: Allosaurus fragilis and A. jimmadseni from the Morrison Formation of the western United States, and Allosaurus material from the Lourinhã Formation of Portugal, counted at genus level whether or not A. europaeus is a separate species. Referrals from other continents are excluded.
Amazonsaurus maranhensis from the Itapecuru Formation (Parnaíba Basin) of Itapecuru-Mirim, Maranhão State, Brazil. A narrower age than Aptian–Albian is not asserted.

Aratasaurus museunacionali from the base of the Romualdo Formation (Araripe Basin) near Santana do Cariri, Ceará, Brazil. Published ages for the formation differ between Aptian and Albian, so only Aptian–Albian is asserted.
Late Jurassic Archaeopteryx material from the Solnhofen–Eichstätt region of Bavaria; no Spanish Early Cretaceous occurrence is accepted here.

sources.citation: IUGS Geoheritage: Jurassic Solnhofen–Eichstätt Archaeopteryx serial site
Foth et al. (2025), Fossil Record: Archaeopteryx from the lower Tithonian Mörnsheim Formation

verification.scope: Argentinosaurus huinculensis from the Huincul Formation (Neuquén Group) near Plaza Huincul, Neuquén Province, Argentina, originally reported as the Río Limay Formation. A narrower range than Cenomanian–Turonian is not asserted.

sources.citation: Garrido (2010), Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales 12:121–177

verification.scope: Brachiosaurus altithorax from the Morrison Formation of the western United States. Tanzanian material is excluded because it belongs to Giraffatitan.

sources.citation: Taylor (2011), correction to the Brachiosaurus–Giraffatitan separation

verification.scope: Buriolestes schultzi from the Hyperodapedon Assemblage Zone of the Santa Maria Formation (Candelária Sequence), Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. A narrower numerical range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Langer, Ramezani & Da Rosa (2018), Gondwana Research 57:133–140

verification.scope: Carnotaurus sastrei from the La Colonia Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina. A narrower numerical range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Bonaparte, Novas & Coria (1990), Contributions in Science 416:1–42

verification.scope: Coelophysis bauri from the Ghost Ranch (Whitaker) quarry in the Chinle Formation of New Mexico, USA. The quarry's stage is debated, so no stage is asserted; Megapnosaurus and fragmentary referrals from other localities are excluded.
Cryolophosaurus ellioti from the Hanson Formation of the central Transantarctic Mountains. No narrower numerical range is asserted.

sources.citation: Smith et al. (2007), USGS Open-File Report 2007-1047
Smith et al. (2007), Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 151:377–421

verification.scope: Deinonychus antirrhopus from the Cloverly Formation of Montana and Wyoming and the Antlers Formation of Oklahoma, USA. Isolated teeth from other units are excluded as tentative referrals.

sources.citation: Ostrom (1969), Peabody Museum of Natural History Bulletin 30
Frederickson, Engel & Cifelli (2020), Palaeogeography, Palaeoclimatology, Palaeoecology 552:109780

verification.scope: Dilophosaurus wetherilli from the Kayenta Formation of northern Arizona. Historical Asian assignments are excluded.
Diplodocus from the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of the western United States. Other diplodocids such as Galeamopus, Supersaurus and the Portuguese Dinheirosaurus are excluded.
Eoraptor lunensis from the Ischigualasto Formation of San Juan Province, Argentina. A narrower numerical range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Sereno, Martínez & Alcober (2012), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 32(sup1):83–179

verification.scope: Giganotosaurus carolinii from the Candeleros Formation (Neuquén Group) of Neuquén Province, Argentina. An early Cenomanian placement has been proposed, but only Cenomanian is asserted.

sources.citation: Garrido (2010), Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales 12:121–177

verification.scope: Gondwanatitan faustoi from the Adamantina Formation (Bauru Group) near Álvares Machado, São Paulo State, Brazil. No stage is asserted because published ages for the formation range from Turonian–Santonian to Campanian–early Maastrichtian.

Guaibasaurus candelariensis from Riograndia Assemblage Zone beds of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, traditionally called the Caturrita Formation and now placed in the upper Candelária Sequence. The Norian age is consistent with a U–Pb maximum depositional age of about 225 Ma; a narrower range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Langer, Bittencourt & Schultz (2011), Earth and Environmental Science Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh 101:301–332
Langer, Ramezani & Da Rosa (2018), Gondwana Research 57:133–140

verification.scope: Confirmed Haplocanthosaurus material from the Morrison Formation of the western United States. Tentative records identified only as possible Haplocanthosaurus are excluded, and no narrower numerical range is asserted.

sources.citation: Curtice et al. (2024), The Anatomical Record

verification.scope: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis from Carnian strata of the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.

Iguanodon bernissartensis from the Sainte-Barbe Clays at Bernissart, Belgium. Historic Iguanodon species now placed in other genera are excluded, and referrals from England, Spain and elsewhere are not listed here.

sources.citation: Charig & Chapman (1998), Bulletin of Zoological Nomenclature 55:99–104
Yans et al. (2005), Comptes Rendus Palevol 4:135–150

verification.scope: Irritator challengeri, known from the holotype skull, from the Romualdo Formation (Santana Group, Araripe Basin) of Ceará, Brazil. Angaturama limai material is excluded. Recent work favours a late Aptian age and older literature an Albian one, so only Aptian–Albian is asserted.

sources.citation: Martill et al. (1996), Journal of the Geological Society 153:5–8
Sues et al. (2002), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 22:535–547

verification.scope: Itapeuasaurus cajapioensis from the Alcântara Formation (São Luís Basin) at Itapeua beach, Cajapió, Maranhão State, Brazil. A sub-stage age is not asserted.
Majungasaurus crenatissimus from the Maastrichtian Maevarano Formation of northwestern Madagascar. Historical names now treated as synonyms are not presented as separate geographic occurrences.

sources.citation: Krause et al. (2007), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 27(S2):1–20

verification.scope: Masiakasaurus knopfleri from the Maastrichtian Maevarano Formation of northwestern Madagascar. No distribution beyond this reviewed formation is asserted.

sources.citation: Carrano, Loewen & Sertich (2011), Smithsonian Contributions to Paleobiology 95

verification.scope: Microraptor from the Jiufotang Formation (Jehol Group) of Liaoning, China. Other Jehol dromaeosaurids, such as Sinornithosaurus and Changyuraptor, are excluded.

Oxalaia quilombensis, known from a partial snout and a maxillary fragment, from the Alcântara Formation (Laje do Coringa site) on Cajual Island, Maranhão, Brazil. A narrower numerical range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Kellner et al. (2011), Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências 83:99–108

verification.scope: Pampadromaeus barberenai from the Hyperodapedon Assemblage Zone of the Santa Maria Formation, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. A narrower numerical range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Langer, Ramezani & Da Rosa (2018), Gondwana Research 57:133–140

verification.scope: Parasaurolophus walkeri from the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, and P. tubicen and P. cyrtocristatus from the Fruitland, Kirtland and Kaiparowits formations of New Mexico and Utah. Fragmentary material only tentatively assigned to the genus is excluded.
Patagotitan mayorum from the Cerro Castaño Member of the Cerro Barcino Formation at La Flecha, Chubut Province, Argentina. U–Pb dates point to about 101.6 Ma, but only Albian is asserted.

sources.citation: Carballido et al. (2017), Proceedings of the Royal Society B 284:20171219

verification.scope: Santanaraptor placidus from the Romualdo Formation (Santana Group, Araripe Basin), northeastern Brazil. Published ages for the formation differ between Aptian and Albian, so only Aptian–Albian is asserted.

sources.citation: Delcourt et al. (2025), The Anatomical Record

verification.scope: Saturnalia tupiniquim from the Hyperodapedon Assemblage Zone of the Santa Maria Formation (Candelária Sequence), Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The late Carnian age follows the U–Pb dating of the unit; no numerical age is asserted for the type site itself.

sources.citation: Langer et al. (1999), Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences IIA 329:511–517
Langer, Ramezani & Da Rosa (2018), Gondwana Research 57:133–140

verification.scope: Scutellosaurus lawleri from the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation of Arizona. Tentative cf. Scutellosaurus records are not used to broaden its published range.

sources.citation: Breeden et al. (2021), Royal Society Open Science 8:201676

verification.scope: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus from the Bahariya Formation of Egypt (the destroyed holotype) and the mainstream referral of Kem Kem Group material from southeastern Morocco. The identity of the Kem Kem material remains debated; records from Brazil, Tunisia and elsewhere are excluded.
Staurikosaurus pricei, known only from the holotype, from the Santa Maria Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. A sub-stage placement and a numerical age are not asserted.

Stegosaurus from the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of the western United States. Portuguese material reported as Stegosaurus cf. ungulatus is excluded as a tentative referral, and Hesperosaurus is not counted.

sources.citation: Maidment et al. (2008), Journal of Systematic Palaeontology 6:367–407

verification.scope: Styracosaurus albertensis from the upper, late Campanian part of the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada. Broad stage-wide PBDB numerical bounds are not asserted.

sources.citation: Brown, Holmes & Currie (2020), Vertebrate Anatomy Morphology Palaeontology 8:67–95

verification.scope: Tapuiasaurus macedoi from the Quiricó Formation (Sanfranciscana Basin) near Coração de Jesus, northern Minas Gerais, Brazil, dated as Aptian on the basis of its fish fauna. A numerical age is not asserted.

Triceratops horridus and T. prorsus from upper Maastrichtian formations of the western United States and of Alberta and Saskatchewan, Canada. Torosaurus and other chasmosaurines are not counted as Triceratops here.

Tyrannosaurus rex from upper Maastrichtian formations of the western United States and of Alberta and Saskatchewan, Canada. Asian Tarbosaurus and the debated older New Mexico material described as T. mcraeensis are excluded.

sources.citation: McIver (2002), Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences 39:207–221

verification.scope: Uberabatitan ribeiroi from Uberaba, Minas Gerais, Brazil, in the unit originally described as the Serra da Galga Member of the Marília Formation (Bauru Group) and now ranked as the Serra da Galga Formation. The Maastrichtian age is biostratigraphic; no radiometric age is asserted.
Velociraptor mongoliensis from the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia. Velociraptor osmolskae from Inner Mongolia, China, is excluded because its placement in the genus has been questioned.

sources.citation: Godefroit et al. (2008), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 28:432–438
King et al. (2020), Journal of Anatomy 237:861–869
